t: Synonym and Alias Registry: a plain-language overview
title: Synonym and Alias Registry: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Synonym and Alias Registry does and why archives need it. A synonym and alias registry is the archive's name book: it records that 'car', 'automobile', and 'motor vehicle' all mean the same thing. Every alternative name points to one canonical concept, so a search for any of them finds everything about all of them. No more missing records because they used a different word.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Synonym and Alias Registry works
title: How the Synonym and Alias Registry works
description: Overview: what the Synonym and Alias Registry does and why archives need it. Real registries store a canonical ID per concept with a table of aliases, each alias normalized (lowercased, punctuation stripped, common variants expanded) before lookup. New synonyms are discovered by distributional similarity — words that appear in the same contexts in large corpora — and by mining redirect pages and 'also known as' patterns. Each alias carries provenance and a confidence score, and homographs (words with two meanings) are split by domain tags so 'bass' the fish and 'bass' the instrument do not collide.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Synonym and Alias Registry works: the deep tour
title: How the Synonym and Alias Registry works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Synonym and Alias Registry does and why archives need it. Real registries store a canonical ID per concept with a table of aliases, each alias normalized (lowercased, punctuation stripped, common variants expanded) before lookup. New synonyms are discovered by distributional similarity — words that appear in the same contexts in large corpora — and by mining redirect pages and 'also known as' patterns. Each alias carries provenance and a confidence score, and homographs (words with two meanings) are split by domain tags so 'bass' the fish and 'bass' the instrument do not collide. Production registries version every alias addition, let curators promote or demote aliases without deleting history, and measure coverage by the fraction of real user queries that resolve to a concept. The limits are emerging slang and highly domain-specific jargon, which need continuous mining, and true ambiguity where even context cannot decide — those resolve to a disambiguation list rather than a forced single concept. A registry that guesses wrong silently is worse than one that asks.
